links.comparator_used: Unedited (fully automatic) deep learning auto-segmentation vs manually corrected DLS-edited OARs, with manual GT-OARs as reference
links.outcome: Geometric similarity (DSC, HD) and dosimetric difference (ΔDmean, ΔDmax) of non-edited vs manually edited auto-segmented OARs
links.effect: All DLS-nonedited OARs had DSC>0.8 and HD<4mm vs DLS-edited OARs. Mean ΔDmean and ΔDmax were within ±300 and ±3 cGyRBE, except oesophagus and larynx, where mean ΔDmean rose up to 837.14 cGyRBE. Conclusion: skilled manual editing needed for few OARs. Vs GT-OARs, non-edited DLS had good DSC (>0.8) in only 12 of 30 OARs and poor DSC (<0.5) in 8.
links.tradeoff: Auto-segmentation took 2.51 minutes on average, and manual correction added 6.24 minutes. DLS failed in 11 patients with significant anatomical challenges and artifact.
links.quote: Compared with manually corrected, DLS-edited OARs, all DLS-nonedited OARs demonstrated excellent similarity with DSC>0.8 and HD<4mm.
